projectName: Walkthrough Offer Copy and Funnel Signals

results.title: Funnel instrumentation
results.summary: Implemented Phase 1 funnel instrumentation: added posthog-js (bundled via new resources/js/analytics.js booted from data-posthog-token/host attributes the marketing layout emits through a new PostHogService::browserConfig() accessor), data-booking-cta placement markers on all six booking controls plus data-booking-fallback on the plain Cal.com link, Cal.com linkReady/bookingSuccessfulV2 forwarding in booking.js, phpunit.xml PostHog pins with failOnEmptyTestSuite, and a five-test MarketingAnalyticsTest. All validation commands pass (Pint clean; 47 targeted and 113 full-suite tests green; bundle built with every funnel string present; empty-filter run exits non-zero). Gap decisions recorded in implementation-notes-phase-1.html: isEnabled() was not added because nothing consumes it (owner rule: delete unused code); bun.lock tarball URLs were normalised back to "" because this machine's policy-managed Socket Firewall registry had rewritten all 300+ existing entries (firewall config untouched, frozen install verified); the manual dev-server/PostHog checks and the linkReady-per-open verification remain the spec's Open Items since they need a browser and write to production PostHog. — The implementation tracks the spec almost line-for-line: analytics.js and the booking.js Cal.com subscriptions match the spec snippets exactly (autocapture off, cross_subdomain_cookie false, opt-out/opt-in handled after init, named destructuring of the bookingSuccessfulV2 payload with no attendee fields), the layout and booking-link Blade changes match the spec's code, all six placement values land on the intended call sites, and phpunit.xml gains failOnEmptyTestSuite plus the three POSTHOG pins. The five Pest tests cover every case the spec enumerates using the same config()-then-get() style as MarketingDiscoveryTest, and PostHogService is not bound as a singleton so per-test config overrides take effect. The only deviation is the omitted `isEnabled()` accessor, which is unused and non-blocking; the diff is ready to commit once that is resolved, with the linkReady-per-open and live-booking checks remaining as the spec's own open manual items.
findings: medium/spec-deviation app/Services/PostHogService.php:88 — Spec's File Changes table and Implementation Details both call for two new accessors, `isEnabled(): bool` and `browserConfig(): ?array`; only `browserConfig()` was added and nothing in the diff calls `isEnabled()` → Either add `isEnabled()` after `withContext()` as the spec shows, or record the omission as a deliberate gap decision (unused accessor) in the commit body so the spec and code agree

results.title: Offer rename
results.summary: Renamed the offer from "free assessment" to "The Walkthrough" across config (Cal.com slug/namespace → birdcar/walkthrough), the MarketingSite Service schema (name → "The Walkthrough", $assessment param → $walkthrough, serviceType kept), every Blade nav/button/footer/prose string in the spec's table, and moved the Folio page to resources/views/pages/walkthrough.blade.php (public.walkthrough) with permanent redirects for /assessment and /contact → /walkthrough plus the sitemap route swap; the three marketing test files were updated (paths, slugs, Service name, host-404 and sitemap datasets), the redirect dataset gained /assessment→/walkthrough, and a new "no page still calls the offer a free assessment" dataset test asserts lowercased HTML of /, /walkthrough, /work, /writing/ contains neither "free assessment" nor "free-assessment" (two chained not->toContain calls, since Pest's OppositeExpectation passes on multi-needle toContain if any single needle is absent). Gap decisions: (1) the unlisted placement marker data-booking-cta="assessment-hero" was renamed to "walkthrough-hero" with its MarketingAnalyticsTest assertion, since Phase 1 is undeployed and Phase 3's spec never references the old value; (2) the redirect coverage extends the existing dataset test rather than adding the separately-named test the spec sketches, matching the file's convention. Notes for the reviewer: the ideation:execute-spec skill refused model invocation (disable-model-invocation), so the spec was implemented directly using the context map's patterns and no implementation-notes HTML was produced; as the context map predicted, `route:list --name=public` cannot show public.walkthrough (Folio rides a fallback route) — it now shows 6 rows including ANY localhost/assessment, and `folio:list` shows /walkthrough → public.walkthrough with no /assessment row. Validation: pint passed, 52/52 in the three marketing files, 7/7 under --filter='walkthrough', both greps exit 0, full suite 118/118. The page move was done with plain mv + `git add -N` so everything stays unstaged; git reports it as R079 assessment.blade.php → walkthrough.blade.php. .ai/rules/resources.md still carries the stale "free assessment" wording by design (Phase 3 owns it). Cal.com event birdcar/walkthrough does not exist yet, so the local embed and fallback link break until the Phase 4 gate; do not deploy this phase alone. — The Phase 2 rename is complete and faithful to the spec: config slugs, the `MarketingSite::head()` parameter and Service name, the Folio `git mv` to `walkthrough.blade.php` with `name('public.walkthrough')` (matching the `work.blade.php` pattern), both `permanentRedirect` entries in the marketing route group, the sitemap route list, and every prose string in the spec's table land exactly as written, with CSS classes/ids correctly left alone. Tests cover all required cases (301 redirects for `/assessment` and `/contact`, the lower-cased no-old-name negative test across four pages, new slug/namespace assertions, `The Walkthrough` schema name, host-404 dataset), and a working-tree grep confirms no remaining `public.assessment`, `free-assessment`, or prose 'free assessment' in app/config/routes/views/tests. Two low, non-blocking notes (an unlisted analytics placement rename and a stale .impeccable surface doc); ready to commit.
findings: low/spec-deviation resources/views/pages/walkthrough.blade.php:14 — Renames the Phase 1 analytics placement marker `assessment-hero` → `walkthrough-hero` (and updates tests/Feature/MarketingAnalyticsTest.php:36 to match); the spec's string table and the Analytics test row ("Request /walkthrough instead of /assessment") do not list this change, and it alters the `placement` property value emitted to PostHog. Harmless today since Phases 1–3 deploy together and nothing else references the old value → Either keep and note it in the commit message so any PostHog insight built for Phase 1 uses `walkthrough-hero`, or revert to `assessment-hero` to match the spec literally.

results.title: Conversion copy and records
results.summary: Rewrote the homepage, walkthrough page, and closing-invitation copy per the spec (reader-subject sentences, two NEPQ questions, three-business-day turnaround, no-pitch line, fit disqualifier, "Where I'd start", paid-week sentence, GitHub/Heroku/Zapier, new replacing-my-team FAQ), added fourteen anchor assertions plus the `speaks to the reader` ratio test and `asks the reader` question test with a `marketingProse()` helper, and updated PRODUCT.md and .ai/rules/resources.md records. All validation commands pass (pint clean; 55/55 marketing tests, 121/121 full suite; both contract filters run non-empty; scarcity grep clean; "three business days" recorded); ratio landed at 24:20 on `/` and 40:37 on `/walkthrough` using the spec's named step-two flip to avoid a 39:39 tie. Gap decisions (tags→space in the helper instead of strip_tags, direct edit of resources.md because record-rule only appends, amending PRODUCT.md lines 79-85/100-103 and resources.md:15 to remove contradictions with the new bullets) are recorded in implementation-notes-phase-3.html. Note: the ideation:execute-spec skill is blocked from model invocation, so the spec was implemented directly under the engine overrides. — The implementation matches the Phase 3 spec closely: every copy block in the three templates is the spec's text, all fourteen anchors plus the retained constraint assertions are in place, both new Pest tests carry the required name phrases, and both record files were updated with frontmatter preserved. The one substantive gap is the missing `assertOk()` in the ratio test, which could let an error page pass on a 0 >= 0 comparison; the remaining findings are a sanctioned-but-unverified fallback wording in walkthrough step two and small record edits beyond the spec's named sections. Ready to commit once `assertOk()` is added and the test suite plus `pint --dirty` are run.
